subproblem.title: Orthonormal basis adapted to a linear functional on ℝ^P
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let β : ℝ^P → ℝ be a continuous linear functional (Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) with operator norm ‖β‖, and let i₀ ∈ Fin P. Then there is an orthonormal basis f = (f_i)_{i ∈ Fin P} of ℝ^P (an OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)) such that for every i ∈ Fin P, β(f_i) = ‖β‖ if i = i₀ and β(f_i) = 0 if i ≠ i₀.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) (i₀ : Fin P), ∃ f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P), ∀ i : Fin P, β (f i) = if i = i₀ then ‖β‖ else 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–3 of the parent proof of cmcs_wedge_norm_le (fact (E1): rotate β to a multiple of a basis covector), including the case b = 0 from step 2. The base index 0 of the parent proof is replaced by an arbitrary index i₀.
1. (Riesz representative.) Let b := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Euclid P)).symm β ∈ ℝ^P. By InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply, β(x) = ⟨b, x⟩ for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Since toDual is a linear isometry equivalence, so is its inverse, hence ‖b‖ = ‖β‖ (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map).
2. (Standard basis.) Let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ, an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. By orthonormality (orthonormal_iff_ite), ⟨e_a, e_c⟩ = 1 if a = c and ⟨e_a, e_c⟩ = 0 if a ≠ c; in particular ‖e_{i₀}‖ = 1.
3. (Case b = 0.) Then ‖β‖ = ‖b‖ = 0, and β(x) = ⟨0, x⟩ = 0 for every x (inner_zero_left). Take f := e. For every i we have β(e_i) = 0. The required value (‖β‖ if i = i₀, 0 otherwise) is 0 in both cases because ‖β‖ = 0. This proves the claim when b = 0.
4. (Case b ≠ 0: a unit vector.) Now ‖b‖ > 0 (norm_pos_iff). Put u := ‖b‖⁻¹·b. Then ‖u‖ = ‖b‖⁻¹·‖b‖ = 1 (norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm), and b = ‖b‖·u (smul_smul and ‖b‖·‖b‖⁻¹ = 1).
5. (Reflection.) Let R := (ℝ ∙ (e_{i₀} − u))ᗮ.reflection, the reflection of ℝ^P in the orthogonal complement of the line spanned by e_{i₀} − u. It is a linear isometry equivalence ℝ^P ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ^P. Since ‖e_{i₀}‖ = 1 = ‖u‖, Submodule.reflection_sub gives R(e_{i₀}) = u.
6. (The basis.) Let f := e.map R (OrthonormalBasis.map). It is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, and f_i = R(e_i) for every i (OrthonormalBasis.map_apply).
7. (Values.) Fix i ∈ Fin P. By steps 1, 4 and 5, and since R preserves inner products (LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map):
β(f_i) = ⟨b, R(e_i)⟩ = ⟨‖b‖·u, R(e_i)⟩ = ‖b‖·⟨u, R(e_i)⟩ = ‖b‖·⟨R(e_{i₀}), R(e_i)⟩ = ‖b‖·⟨e_{i₀}, e_i⟩ (using real_inner_smul_left).
If i = i₀, then ⟨e_{i₀}, e_i⟩ = 1 by step 2, so β(f_i) = ‖b‖ = ‖β‖. If i ≠ i₀, then ⟨e_{i₀}, e_i⟩ = 0 by step 2, so β(f_i) = 0. Hence β(f_i) = (if i = i₀ then ‖β‖ else 0) for every i, which proves the claim when b ≠ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Riesz: b := (toDual ℝ (Euclid P)).symm β satisfies β(x) = ⟨b, x⟩ and ‖b‖ = ‖β‖.
If b = 0, then ‖β‖ = 0 and β = 0, so the standard basis e works.
If b ≠ 0, set u := ‖b‖⁻¹·b (so ‖u‖ = 1 and b = ‖b‖·u) and R := reflection in (ℝ ∙ (e_{i₀} − u))ᗮ, so R(e_{i₀}) = u by Submodule.reflection_sub.
f := e.map R is an orthonormal basis with f_i = R(e_i), and β(f_i) = ‖b‖⟨R e_{i₀}, R e_i⟩ = ‖b‖⟨e_{i₀}, e_i⟩ = (if i = i₀ then ‖β‖ else 0).

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree, including the distinguished index i₀ : Fin P. Riesz representation gives both evaluation and norm identities. The zero case uses the standard basis; the nonzero case normalizes b, reflects e_i₀ to that unit vector, transports the basis, and computes every functional value by orthonormality. All steps are justified independently of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Fiber-sum identity for deleting one entry of a tuple
subproblem.statement: Let k, P ∈ ℕ, i₀ ∈ Fin P and F : (Fin k → Fin P) → ℝ. Then Σ_{j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P} Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} a(j, i) = (k + 1)·Σ_{j' : Fin k → Fin P} F(j'). Here a(j, i) := F(Fin.removeNth i j) if j(i) = i₀ and a(j, i) := 0 otherwise, and Fin.removeNth i j : Fin k → Fin P is j with its i-th entry deleted.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (k P : ℕ) (i₀ : Fin P) (F : (Fin k → Fin P) → ℝ), ∑ j : Fin (k + 1) → Fin P, ∑ i : Fin (k + 1), (if j i = i₀ then F (i.removeNth j) else 0) = ((k : ℝ) + 1) * ∑ j' : Fin k → Fin P, F j'
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the bijection argument of step 5 of the parent proof of cmcs_wedge_norm_le: for fixed i, j ↦ Fin.removeNth i j is a bijection from {j : j(i) = 0} onto Fin k → Fin P, with inverse j' ↦ Fin.insertNth i 0 j'. The index 0 is replaced by an arbitrary i₀, and the summand γ(f ∘ ·)² by an arbitrary F.
For j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P and i ∈ Fin (k+1), write a(j, i) := F(Fin.removeNth i j) if j(i) = i₀ and a(j, i) := 0 otherwise.
1. (Exchange the sums.) By Finset.sum_comm, Σ_j Σ_i a(j, i) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} G(i), where G(i) := Σ_{j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P} a(j, i).
2. (Reindexing for fixed i.) Fix i ∈ Fin (k+1). Define Φ_i : Fin P × (Fin k → Fin P) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin P) by Φ_i(x, j') := Fin.insertNth i x j'. It is a bijection: it is the equivalence Fin.insertNthEquiv (fun _ => Fin P) i, whose inverse is j ↦ (j(i), Fin.removeNth i j), and Φ_i(x, j') is definitionally Fin.insertNth i x j'. Reindex the sum G(i) along Φ_i (Equiv.sum_comp) and split the sum over the product type (Fintype.sum_prod_type). This gives G(i) = Σ_{x ∈ Fin P} Σ_{j' : Fin k → Fin P} a(Fin.insertNth i x j', i).
3. (Evaluating the summand.) (Fin.insertNth i x j')(i) = x (Fin.insertNth_apply_same), and Fin.removeNth i (Fin.insertNth i x j') = j' (Fin.removeNth_insertNth). Hence a(Fin.insertNth i x j', i) = F(j') if x = i₀, and 0 if x ≠ i₀.
4. (Only x = i₀ survives.) For x ≠ i₀ the inner sum is Σ_{j'} 0 = 0 (Finset.sum_eq_zero). By Finset.sum_eq_single (with i₀ ∈ Finset.univ), G(i) = Σ_{j' : Fin k → Fin P} F(j'), a value independent of i.
5. (Sum over i.) Therefore Σ_j Σ_i a(j, i) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} Σ_{j'} F(j') = card(Fin (k+1))·Σ_{j'} F(j') = (k+1)·Σ_{j'} F(j'). This uses Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin and nsmul_eq_mul, together with the cast ((k+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (k : ℝ) + 1 (push_cast). This is the claimed identity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Exchange the j-sum and the i-sum.
For fixed i, reindex the j-sum along the equivalence Fin.insertNthEquiv, (x, j') ↦ Fin.insertNth i x j', and split the sum over Fin P × (Fin k → Fin P).
Fin.insertNth_apply_same and Fin.removeNth_insertNth reduce the summand to [x = i₀]·F(j'); only x = i₀ survives, so each i contributes Σ_{j'} F(j').
Summing this constant over the k+1 values of i gives (k+1)·Σ_{j'} F(j').

audit.reason: The prose and one-line real-valued identity match, without an unstated positivity assumption on F. Exchanging sums, reindexing through insertNthEquiv, evaluating deletion and insertion, and retaining only x=i₀ proves each fiber identity. Counting Fin (k+1), with the stated real cast, gives precisely the conclusion, including k=0. No sibling or parent theorem is used.

subproblem.title: Square of β ∧ γ on tuples from a family where β is concentrated at one index
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let β : ℝ^P → ℝ be a continuous linear functional, γ a k-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) k), v = (v_a)_{a ∈ Fin P} an injective family in ℝ^P, i₀ ∈ Fin P and c ∈ ℝ such that β(v_a) = c if a = i₀ and β(v_a) = 0 if a ≠ i₀. Let ω := β ∧ γ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ), so ω(w_0, …, w_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i·β(w_i)·γ(w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_k). Then for every j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P, ω(v_{j(0)}, …, v_{j(k)})² ≤ c²·Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} s_i. Here s_i := γ(v ∘ (Fin.removeNth i j))² if j(i) = i₀ and s_i := 0 otherwise. Fin.removeNth i j : Fin k → Fin P is j with its i-th entry deleted (m ↦ j(succAbove i m)), and v ∘ j' is the tuple m ↦ v_{j'(m)}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) k) (v : Fin P → Euclid P) (i₀ : Fin P) (c : ℝ), Function.Injective v → (∀ i : Fin P, β (v i) = if i = i₀ then c else 0) → ∀ j : Fin (k + 1) → Fin P, (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ) (fun m => v (j m))) ^ 2 ≤ c ^ 2 * ∑ i : Fin (k + 1), if j i = i₀ then (γ (fun m => v (i.removeNth j m))) ^ 2 else 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof of cmcs_wedge_norm_le (values of β ∧ γ on basis tuples). The adapted orthonormal basis f, the index 0 and the constant ‖b‖ are replaced by an arbitrary injective family v, an index i₀ and a constant c such that β(v_a) = c if a = i₀ and β(v_a) = 0 otherwise.
Fix j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P. Write ω := alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ) and w := v ∘ j (that is, w_m = v_{j(m)}). Write S := c²·Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} s_i for the right-hand side, where s_i := γ(v ∘ removeNth i j)² if j(i) = i₀ and s_i := 0 otherwise.
1. (S ≥ 0.) Each s_i is a square or 0, so Σ_i s_i ≥ 0 (Finset.sum_nonneg). Also c² ≥ 0, hence S ≥ 0.
2. (Case j not injective.) Then w = v ∘ j is not injective: if it were, j would be injective (Function.Injective.of_comp). Since ω is a continuous alternating map, ω(w) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Hence ω(w)² = 0 ≤ S by step 1.
3. (Expansion of ω(w).) By ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, ω(w) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (k+1)} (−1)^i • ((β.smulRight γ)(w_i))(Fin.removeNth i w). The integer (−1)^i acts by zsmul, i.e. as multiplication by the real number (−1)^i (zsmul_eq_mul). By ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, (β.smulRight γ)(x) = β(x)•γ, so the i-th term equals (−1)^i·β(w_i)·γ(Fin.removeNth i w).
Now w_i = v_{j(i)}, so by hypothesis β(w_i) = c if j(i) = i₀ and β(w_i) = 0 otherwise. Also Fin.removeNth i w = v ∘ (Fin.removeNth i j), because both tuples send m ∈ Fin k to v_{j(succAbove i m)} (Fin.removeNth_apply; the two sides agree definitionally). Therefore ω(w) = Σ_i (−1)^i·t_i·γ(v ∘ removeNth i j), where t_i := c if j(i) = i₀ and t_i := 0 otherwise.
4. (Case j injective and j(i) ≠ i₀ for every i.) Then t_i = 0 for every i, so ω(w) = 0 by step 3, and ω(w)² = 0 ≤ S by step 1.
5. (Case j injective and j(i₁) = i₀ for some i₁.) For every i ≠ i₁, injectivity of j gives j(i) ≠ j(i₁) = i₀, so t_i = 0 and s_i = 0. Hence only the index i₁ contributes to either sum (Finset.sum_eq_single): ω(w) = (−1)^{i₁}·c·γ(v ∘ removeNth i₁ j) and S = c²·γ(v ∘ removeNth i₁ j)². Since ((−1)^{i₁})² = ((−1)²)^{i₁} = 1, we get ω(w)² = ((−1)^{i₁})²·c²·γ(v ∘ removeNth i₁ j)² = c²·γ(v ∘ removeNth i₁ j)² = S, so ω(w)² ≤ S.
6. Steps 2, 4 and 5 exhaust all cases, so ω(v ∘ j)² ≤ S for every j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P. ∎
proof_key_steps: The right-hand side S is nonnegative (c² times a sum of squares and zeros).
If j is not injective, then v ∘ j is not injective and the alternating map β ∧ γ vanishes on it.
alternatizeUncurryFin_apply and smulRight_apply give (β ∧ γ)(v ∘ j) = Σ_i (−1)^i·[j(i) = i₀]c·γ(v ∘ removeNth i j).
If j is injective, at most one i₁ has j(i₁) = i₀. If there is none, the value is 0. Otherwise only i₁ contributes to both sides, and ((−1)^{i₁})² = 1 gives equality.

audit.reason: The type exactly captures the stated hypotheses, wedge convention and deletion sum, with arbitrary real c. Repeated indices force the alternating map to vanish; injective tuples have zero or one contributing index. The supplied expansion and squared-sign calculation establish the bound, while nonnegativity handles vanishing cases. Injectivity of v is redundant but harmless. The proof is complete and non-circular.
